newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania arms dump explodes, three presumed dead.
newsitem.headline: Albania arms dump explodes, three presumed dead.

text.p: An explosion rocked an ammunition dump in south Albania on Thursday and three men were missing, presumed dead, an Italian military official said.
The latest report was that four men were also still in hospital after the blast, said an Italian spokesman for the multinational force in Albania protecting aid supplies.

Initial reports said that 14 had been injured in the blast, which left a huge crater and a pall of smoke as it ripped apart surface depots at the dump near the town of Picar, some 18 km (10 miles) north of Gjirokaster, Albania's southernmost town.
"There was a big explosion first...then a huge fire developed. The explosions continued for one and a half hours," said Ligor Koroveshi, the Albanian commander of the base.
He said officers were moving ammunition from the dump when the blast went off.
The state-run news agency ATA said the explosion was caused when someone dropped an ammunition case on the ground.
Ammunition stores all over Albania were looted during rioting and lawlessness which swept the country in February and March after thousands lost life savings in pyramid schemes.
Romanian troops from the international force sped to the scene of Thursday's blast with an ambulance and two trucks and were busy cordoning off the area with Albanian soldiers.
Two weeks ago a dump exploded in northern Albania, killing 27 people, 12 of them children. They had triggered the explosion as they looted the underground store.
